evals.name: landing-page-direction
evals.prompt: I'm building a landing page for an indie note-taking app targeting writers. Describe the visual design direction you'd choose and why.
evals.expected_output: A specific, opinionated design direction: concrete typography choices (font style/feel), deliberate color palette with rationale, layout ideas that avoid generic SaaS-template look; choices cohere around the target audience (writers).
assertions: Commits to a SPECIFIC direction rather than listing generic options or hedging
Typography and color choices are concrete (named characteristics, not just 'nice fonts')
Design choices are explicitly connected to the target audience (writers) rather than generic best practices

evals.name: color-system
evals.prompt: Give me a color palette for a developer-tool documentation site. Include rationale.
evals.expected_output: Concrete palette (specific hues/values or named colors) with functional roles (background/surface/text/accent/code), accessibility-aware contrast reasoning, rationale tied to reading-heavy context rather than decoration.
assertions: Provides specific colors or values, not just adjectives like 'muted blue'
Assigns functional roles to each color (background, text, accent, code blocks)

evals.name: component-hierarchy
evals.prompt: For a pricing page with 3 tiers plus FAQ, plan the component hierarchy and visual emphasis strategy.
evals.expected_output: Clear hierarchy: which tier gets visual emphasis and how (scale/color/badge), consistent component structure across tiers, FAQ treated as lower-emission pattern (accordion/typographic scale), decisions justified by conversion logic.
assertions: States which pricing tier receives emphasis and by what visual mechanism
Maintains structural consistency across the three tiers while differentiating emphasis
FAQ treatment is deliberately de-emphasized relative to pricing tiers with a stated reason
